proposal.hypothesis: A leakage-safe censored watch-time auxiliary head will improve the ranking of long_view by shaping shared representations toward fine-grained watch quality without changing the evaluation label.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit target, train, and model blocks to replace delegated SO.train with a visible torch training loop that preserves the current DeepFM-style shared embedding/MLP backbone but adds a second regression head for transformed watch-time. In build_target, use DV.watch_ratio() on train only to produce log1p(ratio)/12 and a valid mask; keep long_view as the main target and package auxiliary arrays. In model, define a compact shared-bottom network with one binary main head and one scalar watch head. In train, optimize BCE(main long_view) + aux_weight * censored watch loss, where invalid rows are masked out, incomplete plays use squared error to transformed ratio, and completed plays use a one-sided hinge/squared lower-bound against transformed full duration via log1p(duration_ms/1000)/12. Predict returns the main-head logits/probabilities only.
proposal.justification: E003 gives a directly applicable mechanism and loss shape, but the trusted backend cannot consume a new objective automatically. Implementing the consumer visibly in model/train/target makes the hypothesis falsifiable and avoids the no-op pitfall in E001.
proposal.observation: Research record E003 reports that keeping long_view as the ranking objective while adding a small censored watch-time regression head improved official-validation primary over the corresponding baseline. The current parent already uses multitask engagement training with aux_weight=0.2, so extending shared supervision to watch-ratio is mechanically compatible if implemented visibly. Deterministic diagnostics show train_target_phi_with_long_view['is_click']=0.7604858188163154 while other engagement labels are weaker; a denser watch-time auxiliary may supply complementary signal beyond sparse binary heads.

research_evidence.query: How should watch time complement native long_view without changing evaluation labels?
research_evidence.reason: The native binary label discards engagement magnitude and completed plays are right-censored by duration.
research_evidence.summary: Keep native long_view as the ranking objective and add a small censored watch-time regression head sharing FM embeddings. Transform play time and duration with log1p/12. For incomplete plays use exact regression residual; for completed plays use a one-sided lower-bound hinge that stops penalizing predictions above log-duration. Never use evaluation-period feedback as an input feature. BPR plus this auxiliary target at weight 0.2 reached five-seed official-validation primary 0.604023290 ± 0.000282947 versus 0.603517127 ± 0.000631158 for BPR alone; on three random-exposure seeds, unbiased primary was 0.376328528 ± 0.003245064 versus 0.373291085 ± 0.002151737. This is an implementation prior, not permission to replace the fixed relevance label.

proposal.hypothesis: Because both current portfolio leaders are strongly disadvantaged on tab=6, injecting a conservative train-only item prior only on tab=6 will create useful error diversity and improve marginal portfolio contribution even if standalone gain is small.
proposal.implementation_plan: Edit only the predict block. Keep the trained parent model score from SO.predict(model, Xs, split), then load DV.load('train') and DV.load(split) inside predict to compute a train-only item long_view rate prior per video_id and a global fallback for unseen items. Construct a deterministic tab-gated convex mixture only for inference: for rows with tab==6, use alpha*model_score + (1-alpha)*item_prior with fixed alpha around 0.6; for all other tabs, return the original model score unchanged. No labels from valid/test are read, and the prior is constant across users only through the candidate item, so it can change within-user rankings across items.
proposal.justification: A slice-targeted, train-only mixture is a structural residual-targeted change aimed at portfolio diversity, satisfying the stagnation directive. Using tab and train-derived item prior changes (user,candidate-item) ordering on the problematic slice without touching forbidden feedback features.

rejected: A leakage-safe censored watch-time auxiliary head will improve the ranking of long_view by shaping shared representations toward fine-grained watch quality without changing the evaluation label.
selection_rationale: Candidate 1 is the stronger next experiment under the active portfolio objective. It is explicitly aimed at marginal portfolio primary gain via error diversification on a diagnosed weak slice, while Candidate 0 is mainly a member refinement play with uncertain portfolio complementarity. Comparing both viable options: Candidate 0 has better mechanism research support than Candidate 1 because E003 is directly relevant to adding a censored watch-time auxiliary head, and the candidate correctly addresses the backend no-op risk by replacing target/model/train with a visible consumer. However, it requires a full custom training loop replacing the delegated DeepFM path, which materially lowers implementation reliability and raises runtime/shape/stability risk. Its expected gain is plausible but mostly as a refinement of the existing parent mechanism, and the parent already uses multitask engagement heads, so the incremental benefit from one more auxiliary target is uncertain despite being connected. Candidate 1 has weaker external research basis but stronger dataset-specific evidence: both current portfolio leaders are substantially weak on tab=6, the proposed correction directly targets that residual slice, and it is designed for mechanism fusion/error diversification, which is preferred in stagnation_escape with a portfolio active. Its code path is clearly connected because it edits only predict, uses allowed inference-time context (tab and video_id from split, train-only item prior from train), and will deterministically change predictions only on the targeted slice. That gives high implementation reliability, low cost, and high attribution clarity. Although the standalone gain may be small and the prior is coarse, a credible slice-specific portfolio lift is more likely here than with the riskier custom-train auxiliary model. There is no cited exact negative_result matching this specific tab-gated parent-plus-item-prior mixture. Therefore Candidate 1 has the best expected reward after multiplying likely marginal portfolio benefit by evidential/implementation reliability.
